title: Electric Winch

introduction.definition: An electric winch pulls or lifts loads by winding a wire rope onto a drum. A motor drives the drum through a reduction gearbox, and a spring-applied brake holds the load when power is off. Winches haul wagons, pull equipment into place, tension cables or act as the hoist on cranes and lifts.
applications: Haulage of rail wagons and skips
key_points: Rope line pull drops as the rope layers build up (larger effective drum radius)
Keep minimum dead turns on the drum

foundation: Runway beams, columns or pillar foundations designed for the crane wheel/moment loads including dynamic and test loads (structural engineer sign-off).
alignment: Align the first sheave with the drum centre so the fleet angle stays within the maker's limit (typically about 0.5–1.5° plain drum, up to ~2° grooved — check maker).
piping: Power supply via conductor rails, festoon or cable reel; mainline isolator accessible; pendant or radio control labelled with directions.
commissioning: Function-test all motions and limit switches (hoist upper/lower, travel); check brakes; proof load test and thorough examination by a competent person before first use, per the applicable standard and local regulations.

overhaul.task: Overhaul gearbox and brake; replace rope.

lubrication: Gearbox oil; drum bearings greased; rope dressing.

causes: Wear on sheaves/drum, overload, poor spooling
remedies: Inspect and discard per criteria (ISO 4309); correct reeving

causes: Fleet angle too large, slack rope

safety: Stand clear of the rope line (snap-back zone); never step over a tensioned rope.

video_tutorials.title: Electric Winch — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Electric Winch.
An electric winch pulls or lifts loads by winding a wire rope onto a drum.
A motor drives the drum through a reduction gearbox, and a spring-applied brake holds the load when power is off.
Winches haul wagons, pull equipment into place, tension cables or act as the hoist on cranes and lifts.
Typical applications include haulage of rail wagons and skips; mooring and marine handling; construction and erection pulling; hoist drives.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Rope Drum (grooved) with Wound Wire Rope.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Electric Winch — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Electric Winch.
Check brake, rope spooling and dead turns.
Inspect rope; check gearbox oil.
Overhaul gearbox and brake; replace rope.
Watch for wire rope damage: broken wires, kinks, corrosion. Common cause: wear on sheaves/drum, overload, poor spooling.
Watch for brake failure: load drift, increased stopping distance. Common cause: worn linings, contamination, wrong adjustment.
Watch for overload: trip of limiter, structural deformation. Common cause: unknown load weight, side pulling.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
